sections.label: COVID-19 support package
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced a $4 billion package to cushion near-term uncertainties caused by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced a $4 billion package to cushion the near-term uncertainties caused by COVID-19.

sections.label: Tourism and self-employed support
sections.summary: STB formed a Tourism Recovery Action Task Force, and MOM, MOT, MTI, NTUC and MCCY will roll out measures for self-employed persons, including training allowance.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For instance, the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) acted quickly to form the Tourism Recovery Action Task Force, comprising tourism leaders from the private and public sectors to map out recovery strategies.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: MOM, MOT, MTI, NTUC and MCCY will roll out measures to help self-employed persons of multiple sectors, including allowance for training.

sections.label: Citizen-led sustainability workgroups
sections.summary: MEWR is catalysing citizen-led initiatives to address sustainability challenges through its two Citizens' Workgroups.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: As part of its response, MEWR is catalysing citizen-led initiatives to address our sustainability challenges through its two Citizens' Workgroups.

sections.label: Skills, cityscape, Smart Nation, social support
sections.summary: MOE and MOM scale up SkillsFuture and Mid-Career Support; MND, PMO, MOE and MSF set out plans on cityscape, Smart Nation and UPLIFT social support.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: To give Singaporeans a good head start and realise their full potential through their careers, MOE and MOM are working with industry leaders, private training providers and professionals to scale up their respective SkillsFuture programmes and Mid-Career Support Package.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Responding to Mr Arasu Duraisamy's and Mr Saktiandi Supaat's queries on the future of our cityscape, MND spoke about plans to partner Singaporeans to re-design, redevelop and rejuvenate Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In the digital realm, Mr Vikram Nair and Ms Tin Pei Ling painted a vision of a Smart Nation with citizens at its centre and PMO shared how Singaporeans can be involved in the entire process of building our Smart Nation, from conceptualising to deploying digital products and services.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Members like Mr Ang Wei Neng, Assoc Prof Daniel Goh, Miss Cheryl Chan and Ms Rahayu Mahzam agree that we want to create a society with more opportunities for all, whether for children and youths in disadvantaged families, persons with special needs, or working mothers who shoulder a disproportionate amount of care-taking responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: MOE and MSF shared how they are working with corporates, individuals and community stakeholders to co-create and deliver services that will strengthen our social support for disadvantaged groups through the UPLIFT programme, and allow all Singaporeans to participate fully as contributing members of society.

sections.label: Mental health and new citizen integration
sections.summary: MSF is working with Singaporeans in the Youth Mental Well-being Action Group, and the Ministry will partner citizens to co-create Singapore Citizenship Journey content.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Ms Anthea Ong's and Mr Murali Pillai's calls to focus on mental health were answered by MSF, which is working with interested Singaporeans in the Youth Mental Well-being Action Group.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: My Ministry also agrees with Mr Pritam Singh that more can be done for the integration of new citizens, and we will be partnering citizens to co-create content for the Singapore Citizenship Journey, so that new citizens share the same understanding of what it means to be Singaporean.

sections.label: Food sustainability and novel foods
sections.summary: Minister Masagos Zulkifli spoke at MEWR's Committee of Supply about food sustainability amidst climate change and the possible role of novel foods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: This time, it sneaked into the MEWR's Committee of Supply (COS) in the guise of a "fake cow".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We learnt from him – Minister Masagos Zulkifli, not the cow – about how critical it is to have food sustainability amidst climate change and why novel foods may play a big part in this effort.

sections.label: Cell-cultured shrimps and barramundis
sections.summary: MEWR introduced cell-cultured shrimps from Shiok Meats and barramundis from Barramundi Asia, Singapore's first and only deep sea fish farm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: MEWR introduced us to cell-cultured shrimps from the local start-up, Shiok Meats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We learnt about barramundis from Barramundi Asia, Singapore's first and only deep sea fish farm.

sections.label: Tragedy of the commons
sections.summary: The tragedy of the commons is happening right before our eyes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The tragedy of the commons is happening right before our eyes.

sections.label: Trade-offs me versus we
sections.summary: The speaker says the trade-off is me versus we, today versus tomorrow, and we cannot always have the cake and eat it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: As I had shared in previous years' summations, this is what we need to trade off: me versus we, today versus tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We cannot always have the cake and eat it because that is real life.

sections.label: Lifelong learning and COVID-19
sections.summary: Present abilities to manage COVID-19 reflect lifelong learning from SARS and H1N1, and investments such as stockpiled masks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Our present abilities to manage COVID-19 are totally reflective of lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Because of SARS, we resolved to make sure that the 33 who lost their lives did not do so in vain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We learnt – we learnt from others, we practised, we learned again – during H1N1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And all these allowed us to put up a good solid response today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And we did not just learn, we spent and invested for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We stockpiled masks, we kept replenishing and refreshing our stock.

sections.label: Prudence and savings funding response
sections.summary: Prudence and savings allow funding to deal with this event that dropped on our laps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: With our prudence and savings, we are able to fund and deal with this event that just dropped on our laps.
